title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-27
notes:
West leads the ♥Q against 6♠. South has a potential loser in diamonds if the ♦Q is in East's hand. There is also the danger of losing a trick to the ♠K.

Looking at the trump suit in isolation, the best play is to cash the ♠A, hoping one of the defenders has a singleton ♠K. This play is slightly better than finessing in spades. The correct way to play this hand, however, involves finessing in spades. Declarer should first eliminate hearts and clubs, ruffing the third round.

South should now lead a spade towards the dummy. If West follows low, a low spade is played from North. Regardless of the position of the ♠K, the contract is secure. If West has the ♠K, there will be no trump loser. South doesn't mind losing to the ♠K in East's hand because East will be endplayed.

A heart or a club return will provide a ruff and discard taking care of South's diamond loser. A diamond return into North's tenace will be equally fatal. If West shows out when a spade is played, the ♠A is played from North. East is put on lead with the ♠K and again he is endplayed.
